lessonInput.title: Functions and scope
lessonInput.objectives: Use only the supplied claims to make a defensible distinction without adding outside facts.
lessonInput.topics: Claim 0: A function is a named, reusable block of code defined with def that runs only when it is called; variables created inside it are local to that call. Claim 1: A function is defined with the def keyword, a name, parentheses, and a colon, with an indented body. Claim 2: A variable's scope is the part of the program where it can be accessed. Claim 3: A variable created inside a function has local scope and cannot be accessed outside the function. Claim 4: A variable created outside any function has global scope and can be accessed anywhere in the program.
lessonInput.readings: OpenStax Introduction to Python Programming, §6.1 Defining functions; §6.3 Variable scope

scenario.su: A programmer defines a function named calculate_total that uses a variable initialized outside the function. The programmer attempts to read this variable inside the function but receives an error because the variable is not accessible. The constraint is that the function must be reusable across different parts of the program.
scenario.ma:
Program snippet 1: def my_func(): x = 10
Program snippet 2: def another_func(): print(x)

mc.q: When a variable is created inside a function, what is its scope and what is the consequence for external access?
op: It has global scope and can be accessed anywhere in the program.
It has local scope and cannot be accessed outside the function.
It has global scope and can be accessed anywhere in the program.
It has local scope and can be accessed anywhere in the program.
mc.ex: A variable created inside a function has local scope and cannot be accessed outside the function, then correct the closest distractor.

mc.q: Given a variable defined outside any function, what is its scope and how can it be accessed?

It has global scope and can be accessed anywhere in the program.
It has local scope and can be accessed anywhere in the program.
It has global scope and cannot be accessed anywhere in the program.
mc.ex: A variable created outside any function has global scope and can be accessed anywhere in the program, then correct the closest distractor.

scenario.su: A reviewer must label two variables by scope before a deadline, using their creation locations as the constraint. One variable is created inside a function, while the other is created outside any function.
scenario.ma: the inside-function variable-creation record, the outside-function variable-creation record, the local-scope notation, the global-scope notation

mc.q: A review compares a variable created inside a function with one created outside any function; which distinction between local scope and global scope is supported?
op: Inside is local; outside is local
Inside is global; outside is local
Inside is local; outside is global
Inside is global; outside is global
mc.ex: Creation inside a function supports local scope, while creation outside any function supports global scope. Assigning global scope inside and local scope outside reverses both supplied relations.

mc.q: A code passage shows def, a name, parentheses, a colon, and an indented body; under a deadline, how should the reviewer classify this observed structure?
op: It matches the variable scope description
It matches the function call condition
It matches the global scope description
It matches the function definition form
mc.ex: The observed def keyword, name, parentheses, colon, and indented body are the supplied components of a function definition. A function call concerns when the defined block runs, not this defining structure.

lessonInput.title: Seventh-chord functions
lessonInput.objectives: Use only the supplied claims to make a defensible distinction without adding outside facts.
lessonInput.topics: Claim 0: A seventh chord adds a seventh above a triad, and its function depends on its scale degree and its pull within a tonal progression. Claim 1: The supertonic seventh chord functions as a terminal pre-dominant with a strong pull toward the dominant. Claim 2: Adding a seventh to the dominant increases the chord's pull toward the tonic.

scenario.su: A composer is analyzing a progression where the supertonic seventh chord appears before the dominant chord. The composer must determine the chord's role in the progression while adhering to the tonal pull constraints of the key. The constraint is that the analysis must rely solely on the stated functions of these specific chords.
scenario.ma: Compare the function of the supertonic seventh chord as a terminal pre-dominant with the function of adding a seventh to the dominant chord to determine the resulting tonal pull.

mc.q: When analyzing a progression, how does the function of a seventh chord differ when it is the supertonic seventh chord compared to when a seventh is added to the dominant chord?
op: The supertonic seventh chord functions as a terminal pre-dominant while the dominant seventh chord increases pull toward the tonic.
The supertonic seventh chord always increases pull toward the tonic while the dominant seventh chord is a terminal pre-dominant.
Both chords function identically as terminal pre-dominants regardless of their scale degree.
The dominant seventh chord functions as a terminal pre-dominant while the supertonic seventh chord increases pull toward the tonic.
mc.ex: The supertonic seventh chord functions as a terminal pre-dominant with a strong pull toward the dominant, while adding a seventh to the dominant increases the chord's pull toward the tonic, which supports the first option.

mc.q: In a progression, a musician observes a chord built on the supertonic degree and a chord built on the dominant degree with an added seventh. Which statement accurately describes their respective tonal pulls?
op: The supertonic seventh chord has a strong pull toward the dominant, and the dominant seventh chord increases pull toward the tonic.
The supertonic seventh chord increases pull toward the tonic, and the dominant seventh chord is a terminal pre-dominant.
Both chords have an equal pull toward the tonic, regardless of their specific chord type.
The supertonic seventh chord is a terminal pre-dominant, and the dominant seventh chord has a strong pull toward the dominant.
mc.ex: The supertonic seventh chord functions as a terminal pre-dominant with a strong pull toward the dominant, and adding a seventh to the dominant increases the chord's pull toward the tonic, which supports the first option.

facts: A seventh chord adds a seventh above a triad, and its function depends on its scale degree and its pull within a tonal progression.
The supertonic seventh chord functions as a terminal pre-dominant with a strong pull toward the dominant.
Adding a seventh to the dominant increases the chord's pull toward the tonic.

keyTerms.df: A seventh chord is a chord formed by adding a seventh above a triad.
keyTerms.eg: A seventh above a triad provides a concrete instance of a seventh chord.
keyTerms.mi: Adding the seventh fixes the chord's function regardless of its tonal setting.
keyTerms.cx: Scale degree and pull within a tonal progression determine the function instead.

keyTerms.df: The supertonic seventh chord has a terminal pre-dominant function and strongly pulls toward the dominant.
keyTerms.eg: A tonal progression containing this chord presents an instance of strong pull toward the dominant.
keyTerms.mi: The supertonic seventh chord increases the dominant's pull toward the tonic.
keyTerms.cx: That increased tonic pull belongs to adding a seventh to the dominant; the supertonic chord pulls toward the dominant.

keyTerms.df: The dominant is a scale degree whose chord gains greater tonic pull when a seventh is added.
keyTerms.eg: Adding a seventh to the dominant exemplifies an increase in the chord's pull toward the tonic.
keyTerms.mi: Adding a seventh to the dominant creates a terminal pre-dominant that pulls toward the dominant.
keyTerms.cx: The added seventh strengthens movement from the dominant toward the tonic, while the terminal pre-dominant description applies to the supertonic seventh chord.

scenario.su: An analyst must distinguish the functions shown in a tonal progression containing a supertonic seventh chord and a dominant with an added seventh. The classification must account for each recorded scale degree and pull while preserving the different destinations shown.
scenario.ma: supertonic seventh-chord notation, dominant-with-added-seventh notation, scale-degree record, tonal-progression pull observations

mc.q: A tonal progression shows a supertonic seventh chord pulling toward the dominant, while adding a seventh to the dominant strengthens movement toward the tonic; which distinction matches these observations?
op: Supertonic targets dominant; dominant targets tonic
Supertonic targets tonic; dominant targets dominant
Dominant targets supertonic; tonic targets dominant
Supertonic increases tonic pull; dominant is pre-dominant
mc.ex: The supertonic seventh chord pulls toward the dominant, whereas adding a seventh to the dominant increases its pull toward the tonic. The supertonic therefore does not take the tonic-directed relation supplied for the dominant.

mc.q: An analyst sees a seventh added above a triad and records its scale degree and pull within a tonal progression; under the stated constraint, how should the analyst assign function?
op: Function depends on scale degree and pull
Scale degree depends on function and pull
Pull depends on function and scale degree
Function adds the seventh above the triad
mc.ex: A seventh chord's function depends on its scale degree and its pull within a tonal progression. Scale degree is not presented as depending on function and pull.
